architectural_units.name: User
architectural_units.description: The end user of the portal and applications.

architectural_units.name: Leader Service
architectural_units.description: Central routing service that manages traffic and security between external requests and internal microservices.

architectural_units.name: Portal Service
architectural_units.description: Centralized interface for accessing VWGS applications, also hosting frontend binaries.

architectural_units.name: Access Control Service
architectural_units.description: Manages user authentication, roles, and permissions.

architectural_units.name: Communication Log Service
architectural_units.description: Records and audits all system communications and provides analytics.

architectural_units.name: Scheduler Service
architectural_units.description: Handles planning and automation of system tasks.

architectural_units.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
architectural_units.description: Cloud provider hosting the system infrastructure.

architectural_units.name: Amazon EKS
architectural_units.description: Managed Kubernetes service for container orchestration.

architectural_units.name: Amazon RDS
architectural_units.description: Managed database service for data persistence.

architectural_units.name: Presentation Layer (Frontend)
architectural_units.description: Handles user interface and interaction, implemented as a Single-Page Application.

architectural_units.name: View
architectural_units.description: HTML and SCSS files responsible for screen presentation and capturing user input.

architectural_units.name: ViewModel
architectural_units.description: TypeScript files and services that process data and orchestrate HTTP calls.

architectural_units.name: Model (Frontend)
architectural_units.description: TypeScript classes defining the data contract for the frontend.

architectural_units.name: Server Layer (Backend)
architectural_units.description: Handles business logic, security, and data persistence.

architectural_units.name: Controller
architectural_units.description: Handles REST API requests and responses.

architectural_units.name: Service (Backend)
architectural_units.description: Implements business logic and processes data.

architectural_units.name: Model (Backend)
architectural_units.description: Represents internal persistent data entities.

architectural_units.name: DTO / Mapper
architectural_units.description: Handles data transfer objects and conversion between models and external representations.

architectural_units.name: Repository
architectural_units.description: Handles database access and queries.

architectural_units.name: Angular
architectural_units.description: Frontend framework used for the client-side application.

architectural_units.name: Spring Boot
architectural_units.description: Backend framework used for the server-side application.
The User communicates with the Portal Service via the internet.
The Portal Service communicates with the Leader Service for traffic routing and security.
The Leader Service communicates with the Scheduler Service.
The Leader Service communicates with the Access Control Service.
The Leader Service communicates with the Communication Log Service.
The Leader Service communicates with the Portal Service.
The Scheduler Service communicates with Amazon RDS for data persistence.
The Access Control Service communicates with Amazon RDS for data persistence.
The Communication Log Service communicates with Amazon RDS for data persistence.
The Portal Service communicates with Amazon RDS for data persistence.
The Presentation Layer communicates with the ViewModel component.
The ViewModel component communicates with the Model (Frontend) component.
The ViewModel component sends HTTP requests to the Controller component.
The Controller component communicates with the Service (Backend) component.
The Service (Backend) component communicates with the Repository component.
The Repository component communicates with the Model (Backend) component.
The Service (Backend) component communicates with the DTO / Mapper component.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The system is divided into small, independent, and autonomous services where each microservice is responsible for a specific functionality and communicates with others via messaging systems.

patterns.name: Cloud Architecture
patterns.description: The application is designed, deployed, and executed using cloud computing services (AWS) instead of local or physical servers, allowing for scalability, availability, and accessibility.

patterns.name: Client-Server
patterns.description: The application organizes code into two distinct components: the client, which formulates service requests, and the server, which receives, processes, and returns responses.

patterns.name: MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel)
patterns.description: Used in the Angular frontend, this pattern separates the user interface (View) from the logic and data processing (ViewModel) and the data contract (Model).

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.description: The server (backend) organizes code into layers to separate responsibilities: presentation, business logic, data access, domain, and contract layers.

patterns.name: Single-Page Application (SPA)
patterns.description: The client is developed as a Single-Page Application that renders dynamic views and manages internal navigation without reloading the page.
